criterion_scores.reasoning: All four specifically-probed adversarial questions check out under direct testing/tracing: (1) SessionEnd never logs a genuinely-non-abandoned row — 'resume' is a real SessionEnd reason meaning the same session_id continues (confirmed via official docs) and is correctly skipped; 'clear' genuinely issues a new session_id (confirmed via docs) so immediate abandon-logging for it is correct, not a false positive. (2) the no-jq systemMessage is valid JSON (verified with a JSON parser). (3) the rigor-review jq correction filter handles no-correction, before-correction, and after-correction cases correctly, verified against both synthetic data and the actual production failure logs (6 false rows dropped, 1 genuine row kept). (4) the 'gave up' line only fires when attempt >= attempts (true exhaustion), verified by reading req()'s loop and the selftest's forced-stall mock, and 'nothing after this call ran' holds because no code path catches the propagated exception before the process exits. All 26+39+129 offline tests pass when run live. Only a minor jq-call-ordering oddity (harmless, tested) keeps this off a full 1.0.

All five described follow-ups (SessionEnd hook + settings.json registration, rigor-review correction filter, spine_client readable exhaustion message, both gates' cant_run systemMessage, condensed header note) are present and each has passing test coverage added in the same diff (test_gate_in_progress.sh cases (g) and (h), the new spine_client selftest block). The amendment correction row is present in the actual commit (verified via git show), even though the supplied pr139.diff omits artifact/log changes — a gap in the bundle, not the build. No TODO stubs, no silently-unaddressed AC item found.

Correct file placement (.claude/hooks/, .claude/evals/, .claude/scripts/), the 'deliberate sibling' pattern between deep-read-gate.sh and substrate-gate.sh is preserved (both gained the identical cant_run() shape and identical condensed header sentence), and the shared _run_in_progress.sh helper is reused rather than duplicated. Two convention nits: settings.json's self-documenting '//' comment wasn't extended to describe the new SessionEnd hook (every other hook family there is explained; this one isn't), and the jq-existence check in both gates runs after jq is already called silently (harmless but sloppy ordering).

Lean, targeted fixes — each of the five changes answers a specific, named judge finding from PR #138 rather than adding speculative surface. No duplicated state (the SessionEnd sweep reuses the same STATE_DIR/log files and the same already_logged log-once guard as the SessionStart sweep — verified this doesn't double-log via test (g) and by tracing the events-blob dedup key). No tombstoned decision resurrected, no hardcoded secrets, no orphan metrics. The readable retry-exhaustion message is proportionate (one line, not a new subsystem).

Failures are loud and specific throughout: cant_run() names the exact cause (jq missing vs. project dir unreachable) instead of the old silent exit 0; spine_client's exhaustion message names the method/path/exception and states the safe re-run property (verified true by tracing exception propagation). Comments are honest and hedged appropriately (e.g. 'verified 2026-09-27 in the hooks docs' — independently confirmed accurate, not an overclaim). Two minor honesty-adjacent nits, not overclaims: the header doesn't fully enumerate all skip conditions, and the script still builds a report string in a mode it documents as invisible.

defects.why: The file's header docstring only documents 'reason=resume is skipped: the same conversation continues' but the code also unconditionally skips when session_id is empty/missing. Behaviorally correct (fail-safe — no session to attribute), but the comment doesn't name this second skip path, so a reader relying on the docstring alone would miss it.

In --session-end mode the script still builds and printf's the '## Abandoned gate rows' report, even though the same file's own header states SessionEnd's stdout is not shown ('stdout not shown'). Harmless (the pending row is still durably logged to the JSONL regardless), but it means the top-of-file claim 'logs each once ... and prints them so the new session sees what an earlier one left behind' is only true for the SessionStart path, not the SessionEnd path — a minor mismatch between stated behavior and what actually reaches a human.

The explicit jq-presence check (added by this PR) runs AFTER two earlier jq -r calls (SESSION_ID/STOP_ACTIVE parsing) and a jq -e disable-flag check that already silently no-op when jq is absent (each 2>/dev/null-swallowed). Functionally harmless — set -uo pipefail (no -e) means the script doesn't abort and eventually reaches the correct cant_run message, verified by test (h) — but the ordering is confusing: three jq invocations are attempted and silently discarded before the code finally checks whether jq exists at all. Same pattern in substrate-gate.sh.

defects.why: The file's own '//' field is a deliberate self-documenting convention that enumerates and explains every hook family registered below it (v2-trigger, deep-read/substrate gates, ADR-8 graph router, YED-172 callout) but was not extended to mention the new SessionEnd hook this PR adds. Every other hook family in this file gets a numbered explanation; the newest one doesn't, breaking the file's own convention.
